title: Source tiers, and when one source is enough to answer
note: Read by code (src/settling.py). Tiers as the user defined them on 2026-11-10. Tier 1 is the official note or document itself; Tier 2 is a reputed top-tier publisher's report (an exclusive, or a report of a possible announcement), not the official document; Tier 3 is everything else. A claim from a tier listed in `settles_alone` settles its fact on its own and the run answers at once (Tier 1 is read and checked before Tier 2); a Tier 3 claim needs claims from at least `tier3_need_sites` independent sites (copies of one document count once). Every claim still needs its word-for-word quote, exact address and the code checks; further checking (a second source, contradictions, newer documents) is a separate verification step the person asks for.

1.label: Tier 1: official document
1.meaning: the official note or document itself

2.label: Tier 2: top-tier publisher's report
2.meaning: reported by a reputed top-tier publisher (an exclusive, or a report of a possible announcement); not the official document

3.label: Tier 3: other source
3.meaning: any other publication or site; needs a second independent source

strong.label: the company's own filing or release
strong.rule: an issuer document whose issuer is the subject: its website (a confirmed official domain), its own filings, its own releases (also when carried by a wire service such as PR Newswire)

strong.label: the other party's own filing or release
strong.rule: for a question about an acquisition, merger or investment: an issuer document by the target, the buyer or the investor named in the question (an involved company), on its own website or a wire service

strong.label: a regulatory filing
strong.rule: a document on a regulator's own system, whoever filed it (an 8-K by the buyer about the subject counts)
strong.hosts_note: US SEC (EDGAR); India: SEBI, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Reserve Bank of India; Philippines: SEC, Bangko Sentral. Stock exchanges' portals (NSE, BSE, PSE EDGE) are not read: their terms forbid automated use (definitions/skills/statements.json).

strong.label: a top-tier publisher's report
strong.rule: a report by one of these publishers: reputed, but second-hand (an exclusive or a report of a possible announcement), so it is labelled as a report and not the official document
strong.hosts_note: Top-tier publishers as named by the user (Bloomberg, WSJ, Reuters, etc.). Other major publications (CNBC, Forbes, Fortune, ...) are Tier 3 unless added here.
